subject: Follow-up: data handling & marketplace telemetry for Veridian POC
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@veridiananalytics.com>, Dave Liu <dliu@marketplace-partner.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: data handling & marketplace telemetry for Veridian POC

Hi Olivia / Dave —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about the Veridian POC goals and the marketplace flow you described. I promised a quick recap + a short list of clarifying questions so your security/ops team has what they need to evaluate the integration. See below; I grouped items by data handling / telemetry / legal.

1) PII & retention
- You mentioned user identifiers and hashed emails will be sent in some flows. Can you confirm which PII elements you expect to store vs. forward to Redwood? (e.g., full email, hashed email, user_id)
- Target retention windows you need for audit/analytics? (Veridian suggested 90 days on the call; confirm if that's minimum or strict)

2) Logging & observability
- Are you expecting request-level logs from our runtime (full prompts, completions) or only aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts)?
- If request-level logs are required for debugging, is redaction acceptable (prefix-only, KV caching masked)?

3) Third-party telemetry / subprocessors
- For marketplace billing and usage analytics you mentioned a telemetry partner. Who will receive event-level data? Is that partner listed in your vendor registry?
- We can provide our subprocessor registry and SOC2 report; please confirm whether you need a signed DPA addendum or just the registry link.

4) Data residency & encryption
- Any hard requirement that data remain in-region (US-East vs EU)? For the POC we can pin a region but want to confirm.
- KMS preferences (customer-managed key vs Redwood-managed) for any persisted artifacts?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach our current subprocessor registry and SOC2 snapshot for your security team to review.
- If helpful, Marcus (cc'd) can join a 30-min technical deep-dive to show where telemetry flows in the marketplace flow.
- Please send any vendor docs (e.g., your telemetry partner name / contact) and the Veridian security questionnaire — we can pre-fill relevant sections.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-registry.csv (stub), SOC2-Type2-2025.pdf (stub)

Thanks — looking forward to the next short sync.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Olivia Park <olivia@veridiananalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dave Liu <dliu@marketplace-partner.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & marketplace telemetry for Veridian POC

Thanks Hannah — this recap is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers inline below, plus a couple asks from our security team.

1) PII & retention- We will send hashed email and a Veridian user_id. No plaintext emails should be persisted in Redwood storage.- Retention: 90 days for any request-level artifacts; aggregated metrics can be kept longer (we typically store up to 2 years).

2) Logging & observability- For the POC we only need aggregated telemetry (token counts, success/failure rates, latency per model). Full request payloads should not be sent to third parties.- For debug incidents, we may request redacted request-level artifacts (prefix-only or with user-replace tokens).

3) Third-party telemetry / subprocessors- Our marketplace partner (MarketEdge) uses a telemetry provider (Pulselytics) to aggregate usage for billing reconciliation. Pulselytics will only receive aggregated usage events, not raw prompts.- We still need confirmation that Pulselytics is not receiving PII or full request text.

4) Data residency & encryption- POC requirement: US-only (US-East preferred).- We prefer KMS with customer-managed keys if possible, but for POC Redwood-managed keys are acceptable.

Security requested documents:
- Veridian would like your subprocessor registry and SOC2 report (PDF) — please attach.
- We will share our security questionnaire (attached) with the specific questions where we need answers.

Proposed next step: Marcus from Redwood to join a technical call next week (30 min). Also would appreciate a short diagram showing where aggregated telemetry is emitted (service name -> telemetry vendor) so we can present to our InfoSec.

Attachments: veridian-security-q.xlsx

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Olivia

Olivia Park
Head of Partnerships, Veridian Analytics
olivia@veridiananalytics.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@veridiananalytics.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & marketplace telemetry for Veridian POC

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick clarifications. Short technical notes and answers to the specific items your InfoSec asked about.

- PII: Redwood will not persist plaintext emails for marketplace flows by default. We support a hashed_email field and a customer user_id. If you need request-level artifacts for debugging, we can provide redacted snapshots under a controlled support workflow and with an explicit retention window.

- Telemetry: For marketplace usage billing we emit aggregated events (model, tokens_sent, tokens_generated, duration_ms) to our internal billing pipeline. MarketEdge (the marketplace) receives an aggregated daily usage export for reconciliation. Pulselytics is our telemetry partner for Platform metrics; they receive aggregated metrics only (no prompt text, no PII fields). I am attaching our subprocessor registry which lists Pulselytics (telemetry) and MarketEdge (marketplace orchestration).

- Residency & keys: We can provision a US-East-only deployment for the POC. KMS options: 1) Redwood-managed keys (fastest), 2) Customer-managed KMS in AWS (requires duplication of key ARNs and role trust). For the POC I recommend Redwood-managed keys with encryption-at-rest and in-transit; we can upgrade to CMK for the committed deployment.

- Audit artifacts: SOC2-Type2-2025 (attached) covers the controls for our logging/retention and access controls; we can sign a DPA addendum if needed.

Proposed technical call times (PST): Mon Jul 27 10:00-10:30, Tue Jul 28 09:00-09:30, Tue Jul 28 16:00-16:30. Let me know which slot works and I will send a calendar invite + short architecture diagram (1 slide).

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-registry.csv (contains vendor list), SOC2-Type2-2025.pdf

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai
From: Dave Liu <dliu@marketplace-partner.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia@veridiananalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & marketplace telemetry for Veridian POC

All — thanks, this looks good and addresses most of our InfoSec questions. Confirming: Pulselytics receives aggregated metrics only (no PII / no prompt text).

We can take the Mon Jul 27 10:00 PST slot for the technical call. I'll send a calendar invite to this thread and include a brief diagram of the marketplace event flow from MarketEdge -> Pulselytics for your review.

One ask from procurement/security: can we get a one-page DPA summary that lists the subprocessor names and data categories (PII, telemetry, aggregated usage)? If you can provide that ahead of the call it would help speed approvals.

Thanks — Dave
